messages:
vault-bot: Alert: snapshot-manifest-metadata-mismatch (rule: snap-manifest-sse-check). Detected 7 manifests uploaded without `x-amz-server-side-encryption` header to cold-archive bucket. Sample: s3://cold-archive/manifests/prod/manifest-2026-08-12.json
rachel-ops: seeing restore-tool failures for any restore that references those manifests. the loader expects encrypted object pointers. I'm pausing archival lifecycle deletion for the manifest prefix.
sam-devsec: can you paste head-object and the manifest contents for one? need to see if the actual payload points to objects that are encrypted or not.
rachel-ops: head-object (redacted):
```
$ aws s3api head-object --bucket cold-archive --key manifests/prod/manifest-2026-08-12.json
{
  "ContentLength": 1234,
  "ContentType": "application/json",
  "ServerSideEncryption": null
}
```

manifest content shows entries like: `{ "snapshot": "s3://prod-snaps/snap-abc123.tar.gz", "cipher": "kms:arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:666666666666:key/aa11bb22", "digest": "sha256:..." }` — but loader fails when manifest header isn't SSE.
tom-sre: timeline: replication job ran 2026-08-12T00:30Z -> 00:42Z. there was a config flip in replication-controller earlier that day (PR #1456) to add per-tenant tagging. the controller code path that sets the `x-amz-server-side-encryption` header was refactored into a helper and the callsite got missed for manifest uploads.
sam-devsec: root cause sounds like code regression removing SSE header on manifest PUT. containment: tag the 7 manifests as `inc:manifest-unencrypted=true` and set retention lock. also add CloudTrail filter for PutObject on manifests prefix without SSE-KMS.
rachel-ops: i've tagged them and set GOVERNANCE 60d where bucket policy allows. listing commands i used:
```
aws s3api list-objects-v2 --bucket cold-archive --prefix manifests/prod/2026-08-12/ | jq -r '.Contents[].Key' | while read k; do aws s3api head-object --bucket cold-archive --key "$k" | jq -r '"$k " + (.ServerSideEncryption // "NONE")'; done
```
sam-devsec: remediation options:
- re-upload manifests with SSE-KMS (non-destructive): copy to same key with SSE header if IAM allows server-side copy and CMK usage.
- if manifests reference unencrypted data objects, need to re-encrypt data or re-upload encrypted copies of data objects as well.

we should prefer re-uploading manifests first and run loader verification; if loader still fails because referenced objects are unencrypted, escalate to data re-ingest.
tom-sre: i'll prepare a small script to server-side copy manifests into an encrypted prefix using the canonical CMK, verify signatures, and update manifest pointers atomically in the manifest index. sample cp:
```
aws s3 cp s3://cold-archive/manifests/prod/manifest-2026-08-12.json s3://cold-archive-encrypted/manifests/prod/ --sse aws:kms --sse-kms-key-id arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:666666666666:key/aa11bb22
```
ivy-legal: flagging for visibility. please ensure we compile tenant mapping and whether any manifests include customer metadata that would trigger notification. keep legal loop-in early.
sam-devsec: follow-ups: (1) revert/patch PR #1456 to call helper for manifests, add unit/integration test for manifest PUT SSE header, (2) add a pre-deploy lint that checks replication-controller sets SSE header for all object types (manifests + blobs), (3) CloudWatch metric for PutObject without SSE on manifest prefix, (4) add runbook step: after replication changes, run a quick manifest-scan canary.
rachel-ops: taking lead on re-uploading manifests and running loader smoke tests. target T+12h for bulk re-encrypt and T+48h for full verification across prod tenants. assigned INC-2026-08-12-062.
vault-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-08-12-062  Severity: P2  Assignee: rachel-ops
sam-devsec: thanks team. i'll open the patch and the tests. keep the thread updated with verification logs and tenant mapping. :white_check_mark:
